strengths: Elegant theoretical unification: Connects and provides unified perspective on Ito density estimator, Feynman-Kac estimators, twisted diffusion sampler, and other existing methods through the RND identity (Eq. 12), offering both conceptual clarity and practical versatility.

Practical stability improvements: Addresses numerical instability through analytical reference process (Section 4), achieving O(√Δt) convergence rate (Proposition A.2) with empirical validation (Figure 6).

Flexible plug-and-play framework: Works with arbitrary choices of sampling/target processes for multiple inference-time control tasks (annealing, composition, reward-tilting) without task-specific derivations.
Comprehensive theoretical analysis: Includes connections to prior work via multiple propositions (2.2, C.2-C.5), IS perspective (Proposition 3.1), and extension to discrete diffusion (Section A.5).
Reasonable experimental coverage: Spans density estimation, annealing, multi-target SBDD, and reward-tilting with extensive ablations and appendix analysis (Figures 4, 8, 9).
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: Paper acknowledges theoretical equivalence to concurrent Ito density estimator (Skreta et al., 2024) and existing Feynman-Kac estimators (Huang et al., 2021). RND perspective on time-reversal is known; contribution is primarily reframing/unification rather than new concepts.

Modest empirical improvements with unclear advantage over concurrent work: Table 1 shows RNC with ca=1, cb=0 is identical to FKC (Proposition 2.2); improvements require hyperparameter tuning. Table 2 (SBDD) shows nearly identical performance between FKC (0.608) and RNC-TDS (0.578) with large standard deviations. Table 3 improvements are marginal. Claims of 'plug-and-play' undermined by need for hyperparameter tuning (ca, cb).

Narrow experimental scope: Density estimation only on 10D GMM; no evaluation on realistic benchmarks. Molecular experiments use small systems (ALDP: 66 dims, SBDD: only 20 target pairs). Limited baselines—only FKC and 'sum score'. No formal statistical significance testing despite overlapping error bars.

Convergence guarantees incomplete: Proposition A.2 guarantees O(√Δt) only WITH analytical reference. Without it, Eq. (45) shows error can be O(N) in high dimensions. Theory assumes perfect models; practical impact of imperfect scores unanalyzed. No finite-sample error bounds provided.

Gap between theory and practice for imperfect models: Eq. (27) provides 'exact' weights under specific design choices, yet acknowledged in Appendix A.2 to 'not necessarily outperform' flexible designs (Eqs. 21-23). Suggests significant theory-practice mismatch. Eq. (12) doesn't hold exactly in discrete time with imperfect models; breakdown conditions not characterized.

Hyperparameter selection remains unsolved: No principled method for choosing ca, cb despite being critical (Figure 4, 8). Appendix B.2 shows optimal choices are task-dependent. Contradicts 'plug-and-play' claim.

Presentation and reproducibility issues: Critical technical details relegated to appendix (continuous vs. discrete formulations in Section A.3). No mention of code release. Relationship between Eq. (11) and Eq. (13) important for implementation but poorly emphasized. Experimental details scattered across main/appendix.

strengths: Mathematically elegant unification of existing diffusion methods (Itô, FKC, TDS) under a single RNE framework with clear connections (Props 2.2, C.4)
Comprehensive theoretical treatment with detailed proofs, convergence analysis (Prop. A.2), and extensions to discrete diffusion (CTMC)
Flexible framework allowing arbitrary sampling/target process design (Section 2.3.3), offering potential for future methodological improvements
Honest treatment of limitations: acknowledges instability in naive discretization (Section A.3), cases where exact weights underperform (Appendix A.2), and task-dependent optimal choices (Fig. 8)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core insight (RND=1 for time-reversal) is classical (Anderson 1982, Nelson 1967); RN derivatives for diffusion already in Vargas et al. (2023b), Berner et al. (2025). Unifying existing methods ≠ new theoretical insight

Marginal and inconsistent experimental improvements: annealing shows ~3% gain over FKC; multi-target SBDD yields 'similar performance' (authors' own words: 0.608±0.390 vs 0.589±0.413); reward-tilting has no comparisons to other methods. No formal significance testing despite acknowledged SMC diversity issues

'Plug-and-play' overclaimed: requires careful design of a_t, b_t (Section 2.3.3, Appendix A.1), heuristic guidance with limited validation; stability requires reference process adding complexity; task-dependent optimal choices limit generality

Critical theory-practice gap: Eq. (27) provides 'exact' discrete-time weights but they underperform flexible Eqs. (21-23) in practice (Appendix A.2). Imperfect model case restricted to discrete-time, breaking continuous-time theoretical elegance

Restrictive theoretical results: Prop. A.2 convergence requires linear drift, Gaussian reference, bounded L^p moments; discretization error Δ_N = O(d·N) (Section A.3, Eq. 45-59) can negate practical advantages; no fundamentally new theoretical insights

Weak experimental validation: no error bars or significance tests in key results; missing baselines (reward-tilting vs. other guidance); small scales (~23-atom molecules); Fig. 3 compares only to equivalent Itô estimator; RNDE-IS adds computational cost via Monte Carlo sampling

Presentation issues: dense notation and main text; key practical issues (stability, perfect vs. imperfect model distinction, Section 2.3.3 complexity) relegated to appendices; Figure 2 connection diagram buried until page 7; unclear computational cost of reference process

Impractical stability requirement: Section A.3 shows direct Gaussian discretization (Eq. 11) accumulates large error; authors' solution (reference process) adds significant complexity and computational overhead, undermining 'plug-and-play' claim

Comprehensive mathematical treatment including convergence rate analysis (O(√Δt)), detailed proofs, and formal propositions connecting to prior work
Broad applicability to variance-preserving/exploding diffusions, stochastic interpolants, flow matching, and discrete diffusion (CTMC) without restrictive assumptions
Flexible design framework providing meaningful choices in sampling/target processes with complementary strategies for perfect and imperfect models

Thorough experimental validation across density estimation, annealing, multi-target drug design, and reward-tilting with detailed ablations
Clear presentation of complex ideas with good motivation and comprehensive appendix
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: core contributions are primarily unifying existing techniques (RNDE proven theoretically equivalent to Itô estimator) rather than introducing genuinely new algorithms

Marginal practical improvements: Tables 1-2 show performance similar to or only modestly better than FKC/TDS, with improvements often within variance bounds; when ca=1, cb=0, RNC is theoretically identical to FKC
Marginal improvements in practice despite theoretical flexibility: extra design freedom does not translate to clear practical gains in experiments

strengths: Elegant unifying framework: Recovers multiple prior methods (FKC, TDS, Ito density estimator) as special cases through Radon-Nikodym derivative perspective, providing valuable theoretical understanding

Generality and flexibility: Works with arbitrary sampling/target processes without formula modification, offering broader design space than FKC; extends beyond Gaussian diffusion
Comprehensive experiments: Validation across multiple domains (molecular systems, drug design, free energy) with detailed ablations and clear experimental protocols

weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Time-reversal RND=1 is definitional; practical novelty of efficient computation via transition kernels is valuable but somewhat incremental

Incomplete computational analysis: Claims negligible overhead but provides no runtime comparisons; practical cost of computing R at each step not quantified against alternatives
